deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a derivation sheet. It is Riemann's draft of the 'Selbstanzeige' (author's self-announcement) of his paper 'Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen'. The paper was presented to the Göttingen Königliche Societät on 6 November 1856. The announcement was printed in the Göttinger Nachrichten, 1857, No. 1. The header shows that 'gelehrte Anzeigen' was struck out and replaced by 'Nachrichten'.

The page makes four points.
1. Purpose. The functions arise in mathematical physics. Series built from them do for harder problems what Fourier (cosine/sine) series do in simpler ones.
2. History. Euler worked on these functions out of theoretical interest. Applications, especially astronomical ones, apparently led Gauss to his own investigations, part of which he published in his 1812 memoir to the Society.
3. Definition. The only mathematical content is the definition of the series F(α,β,γ,x) = Σ_{n≥0} t_n with t_0 = 1 and term ratio t_{n+1}/t_n = (n+α)(n+β)x / ((n+1)(n+γ)). In modern notation this means t_n = (α)_n (β)_n / ((γ)_n n!) x^n, i.e. the Gauss series 2F1(α,β;γ;x).
4. Terminology and later work.
   - The name 'hypergeometric' was proposed by J. F. Pfaff for the more general series whose term ratio is a rational function of the index, which today are the generalized pFq.
   - Euler, following Wallis, used the word for series whose term ratio is a polynomial of first degree in the index.
   - The unpublished part of Gauss's work, found in his Nachlass, had meanwhile been supplemented by Kummer's papers in Crelle's Journal vol. 15 (dated 1835/36).
   - Kummer's papers treat expressions of F by similar series whose argument is an algebraic function of x, i.e. Kummer's transformations.
   - Euler had already found a special case of these transformations. The sentence continues on the next page with the Euler/Pfaff relation and Riemann's own P-function method from his dissertation, Art. 20.

There is no computation on the page beyond the term-ratio definition.
errors: No mathematical errors. The term-ratio formula is the standard definition of the Gauss series.

Minor dating: Kummer's 'Über die hypergeometrische Reihe' appeared in Crelle vol. 15, which is usually dated 1836. Riemann's '1835' matches the date of composition and the early fascicles, so this is not a real error.
Gauss's memoir was presented in 1812 and printed in the Commentationes of 1813. Riemann's statement correctly refers to the presentation.
